Let [MATH: n,m] be positive integers such that [MATH: n\leq m.] Given an orthogonal set [MATH: \big\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 , \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n \big\} \subset \Bbb R^m] and a vector [MATH: \mathbf x \in \Bbb R^m,] we define the distance between the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and the vector space [MATH: S=\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n \}] as
[MATH: \Vert{ \color{purple} \mathbf{x} - \text{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} }\Vert.]

Content:
We can also define the angle between the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and the subspace [MATH: S] to be the acute angle [MATH: \theta] between the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and its orthogonal projection [MATH: \text{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x},] as shown in the diagram below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/416ecc062316779973c0a5c1a6921bd6]

Content:
Finally, notice that we can represent the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] as a sum of two orthogonal vectors:

Content:
[MATH: \mathbf{x} = \underbrace{\textrm{proj}_{S}\mathbf{x}}_{\large \in S} + \underbrace{(\mathbf{x}-\textrm{proj}_{S}\mathbf{x})}_{\large \in S^\perp}]

Content:
Note: The vector [MATH: \textbf{x}-\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x},] whose norm [MATH: \| \textbf{x}-\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} \|] represents the distance from [MATH: \mathbf{x}] to [MATH: S,] is sometimes called the vector rejection of [MATH: \mathbf{x}] from [MATH: S.]

Item 8 — Tutorial: The Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace

Content:
Let [MATH: n,m] be positive integers such that [MATH: n\leq m.] Given an orthogonal set [MATH: \big\{ \mathbf{a}_1, \mathbf{a}_2 , \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n \big\} \subset \Bbb R^m] and a vector [MATH: \mathbf x \in \Bbb R^m,] we define the distance between the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and the vector space [MATH: S=\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{a}_n \}] as
[MATH: \Vert{ \color{purple} \mathbf{x} - \text{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} }\Vert.]

Content:
We can also define the angle between the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and the subspace [MATH: S] to be the acute angle [MATH: \theta] between the vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] and its orthogonal projection [MATH: \text{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x},] as shown in the diagram below.

Content:

Content:
Note: The vector [MATH: \textbf{x}-\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x},] whose norm [MATH: \| \textbf{x}-\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} \|] represents the distance from [MATH: \mathbf{x}] to [MATH: S,] is sometimes called the vector rejection of [MATH: \mathbf{x}] from [MATH: S.]

Item 15 — Tutorial: Justification of the Formula

Let's now prove the formula for the orthogonal projection of a vector [MATH: \mathbf{x}] onto the subspaces [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1 \}] and [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_2 \}] given that [MATH: \mathbf{a}_1\perp \mathbf{a}_2.]

Content:

Content:
where [MATH: \mathbf{x}_S=\text{proj}_S\,\mathbf{x}] is in [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\},] and [MATH: \mathbf{x}_{S^\perp}] is in the orthogonal complement of [MATH: \textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}]. Content:
As a result, we obtain our formula

Content:
[MATH: proj_{S}x|= k_{1}a_{1} + k_{2}a_{2}; = (x ⋅ a_{1})/(a_{1} ⋅ a_{1})a_{1} + (x ⋅ a_{2})/(a_{2} ⋅ a_{2})a_{2}; = proj_{a_{1}}x + proj_{a_{2}}x.]
